text:
sam: Heads up — after yesterday's roles refactor I can still click Edit on private projects when I'm only assigned Viewer via the new matrix. Repro on prod and staging.
maya: ugh. can you paste the steps?
sam: go to a project i don't own -> top-right kebab -> Edit project -> form opens. No 403. Worked in local repro with older branch.
lee: @sam can you confirm your effective role in the UI (account -> roles) or is this coming from a legacy binding?
sam: verified in console UI I'm listed as Viewer for that org-project. policy service returns role=viewer for /projects/* when i call GET /v1/effective-role with my token.
ana: (not in thread) probably the classic -> shadow perms migration script didn't clear legacy project_edit flags.
maya: I ran a quick audit: 27 users still have legacy permission "project_edit:true" in the legacy_roles table for that org. That flag is supposed to be mapped to Editor in the new matrix and removed.
sec-bot: AUTOMATED AUDIT: migration-run-2026-03-18 found 0 errors; 27 legacy flags remain as flagged_exceptions. See https://internal.redwood/srv/migrations/2026-03-18 (restricted) :warning:
lee: interesting — if policy service returns viewer but UI shows Edit affordance then either: (1) UI checks are still reading legacy flag locally, or (2) there's a client-side feature flag gating the new enforcement.
ops: rolling back the UI gating flag is an option but want to avoid UX regression. we should fix server-side enforcement first.
nana: agreed. server-side authorize middleware should be final gate. can you `curl` the edit endpoint with bearer token and paste response?
sam: here: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X PATCH https://api.redwood/prod/projects/987 --data '{"name":"x"}'` -> returns 200 and project updated. body: `{ "id":987, "name":"x" }`.
lee: that's the smoking gun. server accepts PATCH even though policy service says viewer. Two hypotheses: stale policy cache on authz service, or permission alias mapping still allows legacy flag to bypass.
maya: i pulled authz service logs: `AuthzV2: decision allow user=1132 action=project.update resource=proj:987 reason=legacy_flag(project_edit)=true` 
nana: so authz still checks legacy_roles table directly. migration left a compatibility branch. we must remove that path or ensure it consults migrated roles.
sre-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: potential privilege exposure window starting 2026-03-18T04:12Z. recommend immediate mitigation.
ops: mitigation plan: 1) flip authz feature flag to disable legacy-flag-check (hotfix), 2) run one-off DB cleanup to null legacy flags, 3) re-deploy migration without compatibility code.
lee: agree. quick patch: set `ENABLE_LEGACY_ROLE_LOOKUP=false` in authz config and restart the two instances behind authz-lb. can we do that in next 10m?
ops: scheduling restart now. will do blue-green to avoid errors. tagging @oncall.
maya: also need audit trail: KMS-wrapped logs for who executed the migration and when. audit logs show migrations run but keys rotated; confirm KMS decrypt success for archived migration logs.
nana: i checked KMS: `kms.decrypt` call succeeded for migration-run-2026-03-18 archive, but there are missing envelope IDs for the 27 flagged rows — sounds like migration didn't update audit metadata for those records.
nana: action items for remediation: [ ] hotfix authz flag flip, [ ] DB cleanup script: `UPDATE legacy_roles SET project_edit=null, migrated_at=now(), migrated_by='migration-2026-03-18' WHERE project_edit=true;`, [ ] add audit entries encrypted with KMS for every sanitized row, [ ] add e2e tests that simulate role shadowing and assert denial.
sam: can we hold changes behind canary and watch for 5xxs? last time authz restart gave a spike.
ops: yes will canary on 10% traffic for 15m then roll.
lee: I'll prepare PR to remove compatibility branch from authz after cleanup. cc @security for signoff on migration audit artifacts.
sec-bot: REQUESTED: please add an eval run spec (prompt set + sample users) so Optimize team can recommend batching impact before full rollout.
maya: pulled the 27 users list into a table in the ticket. moving to P0. I'll own cleanup script and audit log patch.
nana: tagging compliance: we need signed proof of change for SOC audit. include KMS-encrypted audit blobs and DB transaction hashes.
sam: thanks — will monitor and report any further leaks. :thumbsup:
ops: authz flag flipped, canary started at 4956789050, no increase in errors so far. will update when fully rolled.
sre-bot: CANARY UPDATE: 0 authz 5xx, 2 denied attempts as expected (both by users who previously edited).
lee: great. after cleanup we should run a randomized permission fuzz test to ensure no other shadow perms exist.
maya: filing follow-up doc on runbook changes for future role migrations.
nana: done. ticket #SEC-7341 updated with all artifacts.
